recipes.name: Pretzel Dogs
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup coarse kosher salt, or to taste

steps.text: Sprinkle the yeast and sugar over 2 cups of warm water in a small bowl. The water should be no more than 100 degrees F (40 degrees C). Let stand for 20 minutes until the yeast softens and begins to form a creamy foam.

Combine the yeast mixture with the warm milk, oil, and salt in a large mixing bowl; stir well to combine. Stir in half of the flour mixture until no dry spots remain. Stir in the remaining flour, 1 cup at a time, mixing well after each addition. The dough should be moderately stiff and slightly sticky.
When the dough has pulled together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.

Spray a large bowl with cooking spray, then place the dough in the bowl and turn to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a light cloth and let rise in a warm place (80 to 95 degrees F (27 to 35 degrees C)) until doubled in volume, about 45 minutes.
After the dough has risen, fill a large pot with about 8 cups water, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, and the baking soda and bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
While the water is coming to a boil cut the the dough into 20 pieces, about the size of a golf ball. Roll each piece into a 12 inch long rope about 1 1/2 inches thick.
Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease 2 baking sheets.
Dip a strip of dough into the boiling water using a pair of tongs, count to 5, remove it from the water, and place it on a paper towel for a few seconds.
Wrap the strip around a hot dog, place on a baking sheet, and sprinkle with coarse salt. Repeat with the remaining strips of dough and hot dogs.
Bake in a preheated oven until they are golden brown, about 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pretzel Dogs
raw_recipe.description: Soft pretzel dough is rolled around hot dogs, sprinkled with salt and baked until golden brown. Now you can experience the pretzel dogs from the mall at home!

review.reviewBody: We made with whole wheat flour (all I had) and I think that they would be much better with white flour. Even still, really good and a lot of fun to make with the fam.

I cut this recipe down to serve 8 since that’s how many hotdogs were in the package. I used turkey dogs and they tasted great. I also made this ahead of time and kept it in a covered foil pan for two hours in the oven on warm. I was concerned they might come out soggy but they came out great. I tasted one before putting them in the oven to keep warm and actually thought they tasted better after they came out of the oven. These would work great to make ahead for a party. We’ll be having them again!

This was very easy and tastey!! I halved the recipe and still came out with 8 dogs wrapped and 8 stand alone pretzels. I should have brushed an eggwash on them before baking as the required 20 min baking time wasn't enough to get them golden brown. I ended up baking them for 10 min more. Then brushed melted butter on them and added coarse kosher salt. Excellent and quick! My family loved them. Will definitely make them again!!!

This was really good. I made it with some lamb sausage. I followed the recipe's directions for the dough with the exception that I used half whole wheat flour, parboiled the sausages and wrapped them. I took the extra dough and formed it into pretzels, sprinkling half with kosher salt and half with sesame seeds. Both the pretzel sausages and the pretzels were excellent. Easy five stars and will make again.

Great recipe. One step that makes it easier and just as tasty is to skip the baking soda bath in hot water, and instead combine one egg yoke with a tsp of water. Brush the pretzel dog with this mixture just before baking. Pretty darn easy and very good.

These are good as is, but I found I needed more hotdogs for the amount of dough.

I have since just made the dough and made ‘hotpockets’ with many different fillings. Ham and cheddar. Mozzarella and pepperoni. I even made a cream cheese filling, froze it in balls and then put it inside. This a a great recipe for kid’s school lunches or picnic food. We love to make them for road trips!

Yum! My picky boys loved them. I made half the recipe (I only wanted 6 dogs) and had extra dough so I made pretzel bites...these were the real hit. Also, I used turkey dogs which were shockingly good.

These aren't actually pretzels, to make them more like a soft pretzel I brushed it with an egg wash. I don't know what the size of a golf ball is where this recipe is from, but it is definitly not enough to make a foot-long inch and a half strip.

I just made these 20 minutes ago, my oldest says, "these aren't pretzels, but they are still good". They look and taste nothing like a pretzel, but the taste was fantastic! I had a little dough left so I brushed it with a little melted butter mixed with honey after they baked and put cinnamon sugar on them, upon my sons request. They just tried them and they like them also. Great recipe I can see these being requested quite a bit. THANK YOU VERY MUCH!!

The dough was a little bland, but fine. I added sesame seeds on dog and made them "mummy turkey dogs". Note: Do NOT make this with gluten free flour! I tried 1 batch with the gluten free and it was a mess and disgusting!
They were alright. The dough was too thick around the dogs. Next time I will use half of what the recipes calls for to wrap each hotdog.
was so good!! not any exotic ingredients pretty much everything you can find in your pantry!! Really easy to clean! 5 stars

This recipe tastes even better than the store bought ones, and it’s super straightforward as well. I followed the directions and the pretzel dogs came out beautifully. It’s also great to make a big batch so you get a ton of value from your time investment. A crowd pleaser for sure.
Looks like a super market fad! What's the dipping sauce?
I love this
No changes, wont make it again. Didnt taste like pretzel, and the dough around the hot dog was soggy. Very disappointed.

The dough didn't taste like pretzel. It was edible, but not what I was looking for. The only change I made was to make a half batch, otherwise followed the directions. I won't be making this one again.
These are a bit challenging and labor intensive but so worth the work! Yum!
dough taste nothing like a pretzel and had very little flavor but was edible prob won't be making these again
this was so good!!! but there was a lot left over.
